matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After proposing a transformed equation, convert each Roman numeral to its integer value and verify that the equality holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you have a candidate transformed equation, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Accepting a new equation without confirming that the left‑hand side and right‑hand side evaluate to the same number.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A matchstick retains its orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) when moved; you cannot rotate it to a different orientation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When deciding where to place a moved stick, ensure the orientation matches the target character’s required orientation.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal stick from an X and placing it as a vertical stick in an I.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: A single‑stick move may affect at most two distinct characters: the source loses the stick and the destination gains it.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When planning a move, ensure you are only modifying the two characters involved.
matchstick.example: Removing a stick from one numeral and also deleting another character entirely, affecting more than two symbols.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must be a single line that begins exactly with ‘Correct version of the equation:’ followed by the transformed equation.
matchstick.example: Providing the answer without the required prefix or with extra lines before the equation.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer between numerals (I ↔ I)
matchstick.principle: Moving a vertical stick (I) from a numeral that contains at least two I’s to another numeral that already contains an I yields two valid numerals; both source and destination remain recognizable Roman numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to adjust the count of I’s in two numerals while keeping both valid.
matchstick.example: Removing an I from ‘III’ and adding it to ‘II’, resulting in ‘II’ and ‘III’ respectively.

matchstick.title: Diagonal stick transfer between numerals (X ↔ V)
matchstick.principle: Moving a single diagonal stick from an X can turn it into a V, and adding a diagonal stick to a V can turn it into an X; both characters stay valid Roman numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a transformation between X and V is required.
matchstick.example: Changing ‘X’ to ‘V’ by moving one of its diagonal sticks elsewhere, leaving the source as a valid ‘V’.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion via stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Moving a vertical stick can turn ‘‑’ into ‘+’ (and vice versa); moving a horizontal stick can turn ‘=’ into ‘‑’ (and vice versa), provided the source operator remains a valid operator after losing the stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation can be fixed by changing an operator using a single stick.
matchstick.example: Attempting to change ‘‑’ to ‘+’ without a vertical‑stick source, leaving the original ‘‑’ invalid.

matchstick.title: Maintain a single equality sign
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, the equation must contain exactly one ‘=’; you may modify an existing ‘=’ but you must not create an additional ‘=’ sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever an operator change could affect the equality sign.
matchstick.example: Turning a ‘‑’ into ‘=’ while leaving the original ‘=’ unchanged, resulting in two ‘=’ symbols.

matchstick.title: Preserve character order
matchstick.principle: A single‑stick move can only add or remove sticks from existing characters; it cannot reorder the sequence of symbols within a numeral or across the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a proposed transformation appears to change the order of letters (e.g., turning ‘XVI’ into ‘XIV’).
matchstick.example: Rearranging the I and V in ‘XVI’ to form ‘XIV’ without moving a stick.

matchstick.title: Validate source and destination characters after stick move
matchstick.principle: Both the character that loses a stick and the character that gains it must remain recognizable Roman numerals or operators; you cannot leave a character empty or with an invalid shape.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after selecting a stick to move, check the resulting shapes of both the source and destination characters.
matchstick.example: Removing the only vertical stick from an ‘I’, leaving nothing, or leaving a single diagonal line that is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model often proposes a transformed equation without checking whether the numeric values actually satisfy the equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always convert each Roman numeral to its integer value and compare the two sides before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Moving a stick can leave a character with a shape that does not correspond to any Roman numeral (e.g., a single diagonal line).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any move, verify that every character matches a known numeral or operator shape.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Sticks are moved to operators without respecting the allowed transformations, producing operators that are not valid or that change the count of ‘=’ signs.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Apply only the documented operator conversions (‑↔+, =↔‑) and ensure the equation still contains exactly one ‘=’.

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effective removal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes removes a stick from a character without adding it elsewhere, effectively deleting a stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Remember that a move must relocate the stick to another character; both source and destination must be updated.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The required prefix ‘Correct version of the equation:’ is omitted or the response contains extra lines.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Output exactly one line that starts with the required phrase followed by the corrected equation.
